intro: For a resale apartment in Limassol, Nicosia or Larnaca, buying and renting cost about the same each month. Buying is roughly even after five years and clearly ahead after ten, even if prices barely move. In Paphos, and for new-build apartments once VAT is counted, renting is cheaper unless prices keep rising by roughly 2–6% a year. The claim that a Cyprus mortgage always costs less than rent comes from comparing the loan payment alone. All figures as of October 2026, with every assumption stated.

blocks.title: Do not extrapolate recent growth
blocks.text: Apartment prices rose 8.9–10.8% a year in the first half of 2026, but there is no guarantee that even half of that pace lasts a decade.
The model gives the renter the cash that a buyer would tie up, invests it, and compares both sides' wealth after the property is sold.

blocks.text: On a resale the transfer fee is 3% up to €85,000, 5% up to €170,000 and 8% above (on €363,000: €2,550 + €4,250 + €15,440), cut by half under the reduction currently applied. Legal fees run at about 1% of the price plus 19% VAT on the fee.

blocks.note: On a resale there is no VAT. On a new build from a developer you pay VAT instead and no transfer fee; the two never apply together.

items: VAT on a new build is 5% only for a main residence, on the first 130 m² and the first €350,000. Above 190 m² or €475,000 the full 19% applies to the whole price.
Stamp duty on contracts was abolished from 1 January 2026.

sections.heading: Worked example: a two-bedroom resale apartment in Limassol

blocks.text: The average apartment sold in Limassol in the first half of 2026 for about €363,000 (transaction data compiled by Ask Wire); a two-bedroom of 75–90 m² sits close to that average. Rent for a two-bedroom is about €1,450 a month.

blocks.title: Cash needed to buy with a 70% mortgage over 25 years

blocks.text: Month to month this is a draw, and the monthly gap is the wrong number to decide on. About €6,475 of the first year's payments repays principal and builds equity, while the €124,340 of cash is the real price of owning. The fair comparison puts that cash in the renter's pocket at 3% a year and compares both sides' wealth after selling (selling costs 3%, rent rising 2% a year).

With flat prices the buyer is about €3,600 behind after five years and €34,000 ahead after ten. A rise of just 0.2% a year closes the five-year gap. For a shorter stay, the same buyer needs prices to rise 2.6% a year to break even after two years and 1.3% after three. If you may leave within two years, rent.

sections.heading: Results by city: resale apartments and new builds

blocks.text: The monthly gap is rent minus the mortgage payment and running costs; a plus means buying is cheaper.

Limassol, Nicosia and Larnaca sit around zero, and Larnaca and Limassol tip towards renting at a 4.5% mortgage rate. Paphos is the outlier: its average price is high compared with local rents, so a buyer there carries a gap of €280–380 a month. Yield estimates for Paphos differ between sources (our data gives 3.4%, Global Property Guide shows 4.4–4.8% for two- and three-bedroom flats), so the question is still open.
New-build prices from developers are quoted plus VAT. Above €475,000 the full 19% applies, and the VAT does not come back on resale. The Limassol case is the median two-bedroom in our own inventory.

blocks.text: A new apartment can rent for more than the average, so the table also shows the rent at which owning and renting cost the same: about €2,400 a month for the Limassol example, well above the €1,400–1,500 average. Check real rental listings for the building before assuming a premium. Some buyers choose a new build for the permanent-residence route, which requires a first-sale new residential property of at least €300,000 plus VAT; then the relevant figure is the cost of the status.

sections.heading: Houses versus apartments: what the data supports

blocks.text: We found no reliable like-for-like rent data for houses and villas, so we do not rank them against apartments on cash flow. The one measurable difference is price growth.
A house also carries land value and higher upkeep. Ask for rent and sale comparables for the specific house before relying on any average.

sections.heading: Sensitivity: mortgage rate, loan-to-value and other assumptions

blocks.text: The mortgage rate matters most after price growth. The Central Bank of Cyprus reported an average rate on new housing loans of 3.24% in July 2026 (3.18% in June), and offers to foreign buyers are typically higher; we use 3.5% as the base case and 4.5% as a stress case. Each extra percentage point adds about €140 a month on the €254,100 loan.

sections.heading: Checklist: five questions to answer before you decide

blocks.title: Answer these before choosing
items: How long will you stay? Under two to three years favours renting; five to ten years favours a resale apartment in Limassol, Nicosia or Larnaca.
Resale or new build? A resale carries a transfer fee and no VAT. A new build carries VAT (5% only for a main residence within the limits, otherwise 19%) and no transfer fee.
Which city, and how does the price compare with the local two-bedroom rent? In Paphos the gap is €280–380 a month; elsewhere it sits around zero.
What are your mortgage terms and cash at closing? Each extra percentage point adds about €140 a month on a €254,100 loan; cash at closing ranges from €88,040 at 80% to €160,640 at 60%.
What rent can the property really achieve, and what does it cost to run? Check real rental listings and budget about €110 a month.
